correctness.rationale: For a partition with weights \\(p_j=|B_j|/n\\), the grouped W state is a weighted q-party W state. The explicit product vector with local excitation amplitude \\(\alpha\sqrt{p_j}\\) has squared overlap \\(\alpha^2/\prod_j(1+\alpha^2p_j)\\). Strict concavity of \\(\log(1+\alpha^2p)\\) and \\(\alpha^2=q/(q-1)\\) give \\(F_\Pi^2\ge A_q\\), strictly for nonuniform block weights. Equal blocks reduce to the symmetric q-party W state, whose exact product fidelity is \\(A_q\\); singleton blocks give \\(A_n\\). Expanding \\(\log A_q\\) yields the stated \\(1/(2e\,q)\\) coefficient. No finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The random-coloring reduction is a central structural step in the new tolerant product-state tester. The W-state theorem proves that its \\(1/q\\) additive scale is not an artifact of the proof: even the optimally chosen partition has a loss asymptotic to \\(1/(2e\,q)\\). This rules out any universal \\(o(1/q)\\) refinement of that reduction and identifies balanced partitions as the exact worst case for this natural witness family.
